newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end little changed in very thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end little changed in very thin trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed little changed in very thin trade on Thursday with investors focused on the release of economic data and resumption of U.S. trading tomorrow, dealers said.

"We're closing off pretty much exactly where we were last night," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc. "There's not enough activity to say the the curve is doing much of anything."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.17 to C$115.70 to yield 6.723 percent against the U.S. 30-year bonds, which closed with a yield of 6.43 percent on Wednesday.
The spread in yields between the two benchmark bonds was 29 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Wednesday.
Dealings were thin in the Canadian market with the U.S. bond market closed for the Thanksgiving holiday. While trade in the Canadian bond market was light, there was no early close recommended.

Analysts said investors are now looking ahead to the release on Friday of some key Canadian economic reports, including real gross domestic product data and the current account balance for the third quarter.

In auction news, the central bank reported that the Government of Canada plans to auction on December 4, C$3.0 billion of bonds with an unspecified coupon, maturing on March 15, 1999. The Bank of Canada said it will buy at least C$300 million of the new bonds.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.01 to C$106.94 to yield 6.064 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond last yielded 6.13 percent.
The negative spread between the two was six basis points.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.75 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.15 percent.
